summary:
MedAssist is an application that astronauts can use to watch their health and help their team members face emergency situations, even when there is no connection to Earth or when they are isolated from their team. 

The problem is that long-time missions can last about three years, affecting the physical and emotional build of astronauts. If there is no doctors on board or near when a situation arises, each crew member should be able to act and keep a record of what happened.
Additionally, real-time communication with the Earth makes it difficult for them to have long-distance assistance.

Thus, the need for a simple, straight-forward device that can assist in decision-making in real-time, and without internet connection.
MedAssist is, first of all, a software solution; but can also be integrated as a hardware device. 
It reads vital signs (heart rate, oxygen levels, breathing, temperature, and movement) every seconds, using sensors and other captors. When the data is wrong (critical) for a certain amount of time, it raises an alert on the device. A crew member with no medical training then answers a few straight forward questions and gets step-by-step instructions read aloud.
Every alert and instruction is stored in a black box that could keep 10 days of data (MVP). When connected to the base, data syncs.
details:
What it does
MedAssist is a wearable early-warning system for astronauts. It works in three stages:

  1. Collect. It reads heart rate, blood oxygen, breathing, skin temperature and movement every second.
  2. Analyze on the device. If a value stays out of range for 30 seconds, or there’s an impact followed by no movement, it raises an alert. The alert needs no connection to Earth. One tap opens the matching emergency guide. A crew member with no medical training answers a few simple questions, and the app sets the severity (low, moderate or critical) and reads out short step-by-step instructions.
  3. Store and sync. Every alert and decision is saved in a “biological black box” for 10 days. Each record is linked to the one before it, so any later change is detected. When the link to the base returns, critical alerts are sent first.

Benefits and impact
On a Mars mission, help from Earth is slow and there’s no doctor on board. MedAssist gives the crew early warning, clear guidance and a reliable record of what happened. We want it to buy time in an emergency and make accident reviews take seconds, not days.

Tools we used

  • Nuxt 4 (Vue), TypeScript and Tailwind CSS
  • Browser APIs: Web Crypto (SHA-256), speech synthesis, audio and vibration
  • Vitest for automated tests
  • GitHub for teamwork, GitHub Pages for hosting, plus an offline local build

There’s no physical hardware yet. A simulator produces realistic sensor data, including low-oxygen and fall scenarios.

What makes it creative

  • A tamper-evident black box for the human body, inspired by aircraft flight recorders.
  • Alerts that lead straight into the right emergency guide, so there’s no searching under stress.
  • Sync that puts lives first: critical data goes out before anything else.
  • Built for real conditions in space: no network, gloves, and users under stress.

What we considered

  • Distance and communication delays, so everything runs offline.
  • Non-medical users under stress, so there’s one question per screen, steps of 15 words or fewer, instructions read aloud, and big buttons.
  • False alarms, so a value must stay bad for 30 seconds before an alert fires, and alerts can be silenced and sound again later.
  • NASA’s spaceflight hazards and health risks, which we mapped to our features to find gaps.
  • Honesty, so our protocols and limits are demonstration values that flight surgeons must validate, and we state the prototype’s limits openly.
